claims.text: TaVCrW in the solid phase has significant short-range order.
Electronic-excitation effects near the Fermi level may materially affect TaVCrW.
Replacing EAM and TI with an MTP and FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
The MTP+FEP result will agree with baseline TOR-TILD free energies to within 0.5 meV/atom.
TaVCrW short-range order provides a stabilization energy of approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
Capturing the 2-3 meV/atom SRO stabilization energy is required for the proposed method to meet its accuracy target.
The calculations are to be evaluated over 2000-2400 K.
A sufficiently large supercell is needed to prevent periodic-boundary effects from destroying SRO.
Dislocation motion through a periodic cell can destroy SRO on a repeatedly traversed slip plane.
Magnetic fluctuations should be explicitly included if they are significant for V or Cr at high temperature.
An MTP can serve as a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT energy landscape.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution and local SRO environments is a prerequisite for a valid FEP estimator.
FEP obtains a free-energy difference by exponential averaging of energy differences between reference and target states.
Greater overlap of the relevant phase-space distributions allows the FEP estimator to converge with fewer samples.
Reproducing SRO and electronic gap-shift effects will enable the claimed greater-than-80% speedup.
The calculated melting temperature will differ from the TOR-TILD result by less than 10 K.
EAM potentials have limitations in reproducing complex liquid phase-space distributions for V and Cr.
The high-temperature applicability of an interatomic potential validated at lower temperatures cannot be assumed.
The usual GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding or overbinding rules do not hold for V and Cr at 0 K and may propagate errors into MTP training data.
Neglecting high-temperature magnetic fluctuations may cause a systematic melting-point error that a nonmagnetic MTP cannot correct.

contradictions.description: The intervention says EAM is replaced by MTP, but the mechanism defines FEP energy differences between EAM as the reference and MTP as the target. It does not consistently specify whether MTP replaces EAM as the reference for perturbation to DFT or whether EAM remains part of the new calculation.

The 0.5 meV/atom criterion is defined inconsistently: the hypothesis and falsification rule treat it as the deviation between MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD, whereas the predicted outcome describes the solid-liquid free-energy difference itself as being within 0.5 meV/atom.

The hypothesized stabilization concerns SRO in the solid, but the listed validation measurement specifies Warren-Cowley SRO parameters only in the liquid, so the experiment does not directly test the claimed solid-phase mediator.
